decisions.executionNote: Orient both grippers downward while advancing cautiously toward wrench and tape; table height and fingertip offset remain uncertain.
Retry rejected start with much smaller wrist rotation and forward increments to preserve elbow-up continuity.
Advance above the inner pair of tools and continue downward wrist orientation; maintain open fingers and elbow continuity.
Finish vertical approach orientation and advance above wrench handle and tape, using both wrist images to refine alignment.
Make small image-guided centering and descent corrections; align wrench handle and tape between open fingers.
Close on wrench handle and tape, then perform a small test lift to verify retention visually.
Lift and carry the apparently retained wrench toward the tray while reopening and advancing the right gripper to recenter the missed tape.
Carry wrench above left tray area for slot inspection; close right fingers around the recentered tape and test lift.
Wrench is visibly no longer retained; return left over its handle. Lift the visibly held tape toward the right tray area while keeping it closed.
Both tools appear slipped rather than retained. Reopen and lower for deeper grasps, reducing right-arm height to restore IK margin.
Regrasp lower on the wrench handle with centered fingers. Align the right gripper over the tape more deeply before closure.
Test the deeper wrench grasp with a vertical lift. Close around the recentered tape and lift slightly backward to maintain joint margin.
Carry the visibly retained wrench toward its tray region. Reopen and descend farther around the tape, whose previous grasp missed.
The wrench slipped during translation. Retry with a substantially deeper handle grasp; lower open fingers around tape before closing.
Narrow left opening to avoid the toolbox rim and grasp the wrench handle centrally. Test tape retention with a slow vertical lift.
Lift left clear of rim, correct wrist verticality and recenter on wrench. Slowly carry the tape inward and backward toward its square recess.
Approach wrench with a narrowed aperture to clear the tray rim. Reorient right gripper to grasp tape from a different direction rather than repeating slipping edge grasps.
Close left around the now-centered handle after a deeper rim-clearing approach. Finish the right quarter-turn and approach the upright tape from above.
Test the centered wrench grasp without rapid lateral motion. Close on the tape across its new orientation and lift gently for visual verification.
Both tools now appear between the fingers. Carry slowly toward their tray regions with small added clearance and closed grippers.
Raise the retained wrench above the rim before further transport. Reopen and return right above the tape, which slipped against the tray wall.
Repeated rim interference prevents secure inner-tool grasps. Move to the unobstructed hammer and pliers to establish deeper grasps away from the toolbox.
Descend over unobstructed hammer and plier handles, keeping fingers open and finishing right gripper alignment.
Center both handles at the finger contact line, close below their top surfaces, and test lift the hammer and pliers.
Lift the hammer and pliers well above the toolbox rim, retreating slightly to preserve joint margin before carrying inward.
Pliers remain visibly retained; carry them inward at rim-clearance height. Hammer missed, so retry significantly deeper around its unobstructed handle.
Close on the deeply approached hammer and test lift. Continue carrying the retained pliers over the right side of the toolbox.
Lift hammer with greater rim clearance. Open and withdraw right to inspect where the pliers settled in the toolbox.
Carry the retained hammer inward and turn it along the tray's long lower recess. Move the empty right arm clear for slot inspection.
Replan from the continuity interruption with smaller yaw and translation increments while holding the hammer; keep right arm clear.
Complete hammer quarter-turn and approach the long front recess at clearance height; bring the empty right gripper back toward tape.
Align the hammer along the front tray channel without crossing the arms. Approach the tape again from the right with open fingers.
Align hammer head inside the front-left recess and lower it along the long channel, maintaining separation from the right arm. Reclose around the upright tape.
Release hammer at the front recess and withdraw for inspection; lift the newly grasped tape above the rim while retreating to keep IK margin.
Withdraw left fully to inspect the seated hammer. Carry the visibly retained tape above the square right-side recess with full rim clearance.
Lower and advance tape over the square upper-right recess. Return left above wrench with a vertical grasp orientation.
Release tape into the square recess and retract right for inspection. Approach wrench handle with a narrow opening to clear the neighboring tray rim.
Regrasp wrench at the centered handle with deeper closure. Reapproach tape to correct its tilted, forward-edge placement within the square recess.
Lift wrench well above the rim before transport. Regrasp tape and make a small lift/rotation toward the square recess alignment.
Carry retained wrench above the left interior channel. Ease tape farther into its square recess and release to let it settle.
Wrench slipped from the handle; return for a grasp nearer its heavy head. Fully disengage right fingers so tape can settle in its recess.
Approach the wrench head rather than its slipping handle, narrowing fingers to clear the rim. Move right clear of the tape for an unobstructed inspection.
Center and close on the wrench's heavy head. Position closed right fingertips beside the upright tape for a gentle seating adjustment.
Lift left before repositioning over the displaced wrench head to avoid further pushing. Recenter right over upright tape for a controlled flattening grasp.
Grasp the wrench neck after vertical descent. Close on tape and begin a small compensated pitch to lay it flat, backing away from the IK boundary.
Test lift the wrench grasped near its head. Raise closed right fingertips to the tape's upper side and gently bias it toward lying flat.
Raise the head-grasped wrench enough to clear its hanging handle. Recenter open right fingers around tape accounting for the tilted wrist offset.
Carry the securely head-grasped wrench inward and start laying its handle rearward. Advance right to pinch the upright tape centrally rather than below it.
Lower wrench into the left interior, advancing its head to lay the handle down. Rotate the newly pinched tape toward flat with fingertip-offset compensation.
Wrench now rests across the tray; turn left fingers to regrasp its horizontal handle. Recenter right on tape using the larger observed fingertip offset.
Back and lower left to restore joint margin while finishing the handle-grasp yaw. Continue right centering over tape using wrist alignment.
Retry continuity recovery with very small left increments near the folded-joint boundary; continue centering right on tape.
Align left fingers across the horizontal wrench handle. Raise closed right fingertips to contact the upper tape edge rather than its base.
Close left around the horizontal wrench handle with rim clearance. Use a small right-side inward/downward nudge at the tape's upper edge.
Lift and shift wrench inward from the protruding left edge toward its channel. Retract and straighten the right wrist to approach the pliers next.
The wrench recess appears to have its broad end on the right. Lift and begin reversing the held wrench, keeping the right arm clear.
Continue reversing the retained wrench above the tray. Move right toward the pliers at the back edge, maintaining arm separation.
The wrench slipped onto the right interior during rotation. Bring right fingers to its head while moving the empty left arm back toward the pliers side.
Align right fingers at wrench neck and close. Approach pliers with a slight inward left-wrist tilt, keeping the left EE on its own side.
Close left around both plier handles and test lift backward. Lift the right-held wrench by its head, clearing the neighboring tray ridges.
Rotate the right-held wrench from dangling toward horizontal with its handle left, compensating fingertip offset. Reapproach the plier handles farther forward.
Close without moving on the centered plier handles, then test lift. Lower wrench inward onto the middle tray and release gently.
Use an angled left approach to reach the plier neck at the rear rim rather than the spreading handle tips. Fully withdraw right from the released wrench.
Center the left angled grasp on pliers near their pivot. Reorient right over the hammer handle to shift its protruding head fully into the front recess.
